key_insight: Artificial flame thickening has competing effects in turbulent lean hydrogen flames: increased effective Karlovitz number enhances mean local flame speed, while decreased effective Damköhler number reduces flame wrinkling.
engineering_relevance: Accurate coarse-mesh hydrogen combustion predictions require corrections for both local flame propagation and flame area, rather than wrinkling alone.
method: Analyze over 200 flame-resolved simulations with detailed chemistry and transport in homogeneous isotropic turbulence.
Match thickened flames using Ka_f^F = Ka_f√F and Da_f^F = Da_f/F.
Propose an implicit, self-consistent efficiency correction to recover unthickened flame consumption speed.
evidence_signal: Simulations matched in effective Karlovitz and Damköhler numbers collapse across thickening factors until the thickened flame approaches integral or geometric length scales.
watch_item: The proposed efficiency factor must be determined implicitly because it feeds back on the effective dimensionless numbers, and scaling collapse breaks down near configuration length scales.
paper_title: A Systematic Assessment of Artificial Flame Thickening for Thermodiffusively Unstable Lean Hydrogen Flames in Homogeneous Isotropic Turbulence
